note: Weight-bearing bones lose about 1 to 1.5% of density per month in flight. Resistance exercise is the main countermeasure.
Calf muscle volume fell about 13% and peak power about 32% after six months on the ISS despite exercise. Higher load matters more than more minutes.
Astronauts form kidney stones more often than before flight. Spaceflight changes how the kidney handles salts, on top of calcium released from bone. Good fluid intake lowers the risk.
Body fluid moves toward the head in weightlessness and plasma volume drops 10 to 20% in the first two days. Thirst is a poor guide to hydration in flight.
About two thirds of long-duration astronauts show early signs of spaceflight associated neuro-ocular syndrome. Any change in vision should be reported and examined.
Crews are scheduled 8.5 hours of sleep but average about 6. Sleep loss slows reaction time and attention.
In NASA analog missions a night without sleep made crews slower and less accurate on vigilance tests. Safety-critical tasks should wait until performance recovers.
The dose in Mars transit is about 1.8 mSv per day. Solar particle events raise it sharply for hours to days, and a shielded shelter reduces the exposure.
Stress and sleep loss weaken immunity in flight. More than half of astronauts shed reactivated herpes viruses, usually without symptoms.
ISS crews ate about 80% of their energy needs and lost body mass. Vitamin D falls because there is no sunlight in a spacecraft, so supplements are scheduled.
source: Smith et al. 2005, Journal of Nutrition

note: Medicines stored in space lost potency faster than matching ones on Earth. HALO never gives doses. The flight surgeon's schedule decides medication.
Six of eleven ISS crew had stalled or reversed flow in the jugular vein, and one had a clot. Neck swelling or pain should be reported.
source: Marshall-Goebel et al. 2019, JAMA Network Open

note: Isolation and confinement raise the risk of low mood, conflict and poor sleep, more so the longer and more cut off the mission is. Regular check-ins and private support channels help.
